resolved_by: Supreme Court in McQuiggin v. Perkins, 569 U.S. 383 (2013), which granted certiorari to resolve the circuit split and held that actual innocence serves as a gateway around AEDPA's statute of limitations.
issue: Does a showing of actual innocence excuse a federal habeas petitioner from AEDPA's one-year statute of limitations?
this_court: The court applies McQuiggin and treats the actual-innocence gateway as an exception to the AEDPA limitations period. The excerpts do not show the court taking a position on the pre-McQuiggin split.
quote: The Supreme Court granted certiorari to resolve a Circuit split concerning whether there is an exception to AEDPA’s one-year statute of limitations for a claim of actual innocence.
cite: Joseph Wallace v. Superintendent Mahanoy SCI, 2 F.4th 133 (3rd Cir. 2021)
